Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Short answers up front: we can accept a consolidated USD wire, but there are options with different downstream impacts; we can also accommodate net-of-fees in specific cases (see below). To advise properly I need two quick confirmations: (A) exact invoice numbers to allocate against, and (B) the beneficiary entity you want funds to settle to (Redwood Inference, Inc. — US parent, or Redwood Inference EU Holdings?).

Options we commonly suggest:
- Separate wires (recommended when invoices are cross-jurisdictional): one wire per billed legal entity. Simplest for VAT/GST and tax documentation.
- Single consolidated wire to Redwood US (USD): payer provides an allocation/memo that lists invoice numbers and amounts. DBS will likely route via correspondent banks (possible intermediary fees). By default Redwood expects the full invoiced gross amount to be received; payer covers correspondent fees.
- Net-of-intermediary-fees: Redwood can accept net receipts if payer agrees to provide (1) a payment breakdown showing expected gross amounts, (2) signed confirmation that payer will not seek to reclaim the shortfall, and (3) the final bank statement showing intermediary debit amounts. Finance (copied) will issue a one-time credit for documented intermediary fees after settlement.

VAT/GST notes:
- EU invoice: if Meditech EU B.V. is VAT-registered and the supply is eligible for reverse-charge, we can issue an updated invoice with the reverse-charge note and our EU VAT ID. You should confirm your VAT ID and that you’re the taxable recipient (we’ll need it to update the invoice).
- Singapore GST: Redwood is not GST-registered in Singapore for this pilot. We therefore do not charge SGD GST on services billed to the Singapore entity; your APAC team would typically self-assess GST under local rules where applicable.

What I need from you to proceed:
1) Confirm invoice numbers and the preferred beneficiary (US vs EU entity).
2) If you choose net-of-fees, confirm you will provide bank evidence and accept a one-time post-payment credit for intermediary fees.
3) Provide VAT ID for Meditech EU B.V. so we can issue a reverse-charge invoice if appropriate.

I’ll loop in Finance (Laura) to confirm the operational steps and timeline once you confirm.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Team — finance here, thanks for the heads up. We can support the net-of-intermediary-fees flow with these conditions and steps: 

1) Required payer documentation (to be provided by Meditech):
   - DBS payment confirmation showing the gross debited amount and the final net USD received by us (PDF).
   - Intermediary/correspondent fee line(s) on the SWIFT MT103 or bank confirmation that show the exact fee amounts and which bank charged them.
   - Remittance advice with invoice breakdown (RDW-INV-2028-09-014: EUR amount -> USD equivalent; RDW-INV-2028-09-015: SGD amount -> USD equivalent) so we can allocate receipts.

2) Allocation and accounting rules:
   - Because funds will land in Redwood US, we will: (a) apply the gross-equivalent amounts against each billed invoice, and (b) post a one-time credit to the payable invoice(s) equal to the documented intermediary fees (pro-rata across invoices based on gross amounts if fees affect both legs).
   - Expected turnaround: accounting will credit the affected invoice(s) within 3 business days of receiving clear bank evidence. Credits will show as separate credit memos and will be reflected in our AR system.

3) VAT/GST handling:
   - EU reverse-charge: we can reissue the EU invoice with reverse-charge note and our EU VAT ID provided Meditech supplies their VAT ID. We will not apply or refund VAT — instead the invoice will explicitly state reverse-charge so Meditech can self-account.
   - Singapore GST: Redwood is not GST-registered in Singapore; we will not issue invoices with GST. Meditech should self-assess GST locally if required.

4) Operational suggestions to reduce reconciliation friction:
   - If possible, include this exact memo in the beneficiary reference: "PAY: RDW-INV-2028-09-014 | RDW-INV-2028-09-015 | MEDITECH — SOMETREAS". That reference is searchable in our remittance system and speeds allocation.
   - Preferably, include a pdf remittance with the wire that maps gross amounts to invoice numbers.

5) If Meditech prefers separate wires we will treat each as usual and no net-of-fees policy is needed; separate wires simplify tax/FX allocation.

I’ve attached our net_of_fees_policy.pdf which outlines documentation requirements. Once Meditech confirms and sends the DBS wire, forward their bank confirmation to accounts@redwood.ai and we’ll action the credit.

Laura Bennett
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: net_of_fees_policy.pdf
